title: Ethiopian Economics University Entrance Exam 2016
description: Ethiopian Economics University Entrance Exam 2016 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following represents the increase in the quantity supplied of the real GDP due to the increase in the price level?
options: The right wards shifts of the aggregate supply curve
The left ward shifts of the aggregate supply curve
The down wards movement along the aggregate supply curve.
The upwards movement along the aggregate supply curve
questions.explanation:
An increase in the price level causes an upwards movement along the short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve, representing an increase in the quantity of real GDP supplied.

 A shift of the curve is caused by changes in factors other than the price level (like resource prices or technology).

questions.questionText: When the economy is in the long run which of the following is correct?
options: Sticky wages and workers misperception still holds true
What the economy produces is the full employment real GDP
The short run and the long run GDP will the same
The level of the real GDP the economy produces is less than the natural real GDP
questions.explanation:
In the long run, wages and prices are fully flexible, and the economy naturally adjusts to produce its full employment real GDP (or natural real GDP).

 At this output level, all resources are employed at their normal rate, and the unemployment rate equals the natural rate of unemployment.

questions.questionText: What is the pressure on price when the quantity demand of the real GDP is greater than the quantity supplied of real GDP during the short run?
questions.explanation:
If the quantity demanded of real GDP is greater than the quantity supplied (i.e., Aggregate Demand > Aggregate Supply), there is an excess demand or a shortage in the economy.

 This puts upward pressure on the price level as buyers compete for the limited goods and services.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the economy when it is in long run equilibrium?
options: The economy produces the real GDP which is called the natural real GDP
The short run aggregate demand curve intersect the short run aggregate supply curve
The long run aggregate demand curve intersect the short run aggregate supply curve
Price temporarily deviates from equilibrium even if aggregate demand and aggregate supply remain unchanged.
questions.explanation:
In long-run equilibrium, the economy is operating at its maximum sustainable capacity. This corresponds to the output level known as the natural real GDP** (or potential GDP).

 At this point, the Aggregate Demand (AD), Short-Run Aggregate Supply (SRAS), and Long-Run Aggregate Supply (LRAS) curves all intersect.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is represent economic situation where there is an inefficient distribution of goods and services in the free markets?
questions.explanation:
A market failure is a situation where the allocation of goods and services by a free market is not efficient.

 Externalities, asymmetric information, and the free-rider problem (related to public goods) are all common causes or examples of market failure.

questions.questionText: What impacts on our aggregate demand do you expect if the level of economic activities in other countries increase?
options: Aggregate demand first declines and then rises
questions.explanation:
An increase in economic activity in other countries means their incomes are rising. This typically leads to them buying more of our goods and services (i.e., our exports increase).

 Since Net Exports (X - M) are a component of Aggregate Demand (AD) (AD = C + I + G + (X - M)), an increase in exports causes the Aggregate Demand curve to shift to the right (increase).

questions.questionText: Among the following which one differentiates changes in quantity demanded from change in aggregate demand?
options: As price level falls, the quantity demanded real GDP rises, ceteris paribus
It represented as the movement from one points to another along the different demand curve
A positive change in any factors causes a right ward shift in the AD curve
It is a shift in Aggregate demand curve from AD1 to AD2 on different curve
questions.explanation:
A change in quantity demanded (or quantity of real GDP demanded) is caused only by a change in the price level and is shown as a movement along the Aggregate Demand (AD) curve.

 A change in aggregate demand is caused by a change in any non-price factor (like C, I, G, or X-M) and is shown as a shift of the entire AD curve.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about Aggregate demand curve?
options: It represent the inverse relationship between the real GDP demand and consumption expenditure, all else being equal.
It's a schedule that represents the amount of real output that sellers collectively desire to sell at each price, ceteris paribus.
It shows the inverse relationship between the amount of real output buyers desire to buy at each price, all else being equal.
It shows the inverse relationship between the amount of real output sellers desire to sell at each price, all else being equal.
questions.explanation:
The Aggregate Demand (AD) curve shows the inverse relationship between the price level and the quantity of real GDP that households, firms, government, and foreign buyers collectively desire to buy.

 This inverse relationship is due to the wealth effect, interest rate effect, and net export effect.

questions.questionText: What is the implication of the Keynesian Horizontal aggregate supply curve?
options: Firms can supply whatever amount demand at the existing price because of unemployment.
Firms can obtain much labor as they want as long as they pay more
As output level changes, the average cost of production increases
The labor market in equilibrium with full employment of the labor force
questions.explanation:
The Keynesian Horizontal Aggregate Supply (AS) curve (or extreme short-run view) assumes that the economy is far below its full-employment level (deep recession).

 In this scenario, there are vast idle resources (like high unemployment), meaning firms can increase output significantly without having to raise prices or average costs.

 Thus, output is perfectly elastic with respect to the price level.

questions.questionText: 10) Which one of the following is the main factor that affect the amount of output firms are willing to supply?
options: The price related to goods produced by other firms
The price they receive for their goods
The level of the economic activity in other countries
The prices they anticipate to prevail in the future
questions.explanation:
In microeconomics, the price a firm receives for its good is the primary determinant of the quantity supplied, as it directly impacts profit.

 In macroeconomics, the general price level is the main factor influencing the quantity of real GDP supplied in the short run (moving along the SRAS curve).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not the cause of market failure?
questions.explanation:
Private goods (goods that are rivalrous and excludable) are typically allocated efficiently by competitive markets.

 Market failures occur due to issues like Monopoly (market power), Externalities (side effects), Factors immobility (inability to reallocate resources efficiently), and Public Goods (non-excludability and non-rivalry).

questions.questionText: Suppose Sol-tech Company receives positive externalities from COMP educated graduate subsidized company for education through scholarship. In which of the following group this type of solution for market failure listed?
questions.explanation:
The scenario describes a subsidy (scholarship) provided by a company (COMP) to encourage the production of a positive externality (educated graduates).

 This is an example of a Private market solution (or private bargaining/donation/subsidy) to internalize an externality, as it involves non-government entities addressing the issue through market mechanisms.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of public goods?
questions.explanation:
Public goods are characterized by non-rivalry and non-excludability.

 Wilderness (like open parks or scenic views) often exhibits these characteristics. Houses, Food items, and Clothes are all **private goods** (rivalrous and excludable).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following characterize public goods?
questions.explanation: The defining characteristics of a pure public good are non-rivalry (one person consuming it does not prevent another from consuming it) and non-excludability (it is impossible or too costly to prevent non-payers from using it).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following factor is the reason for market inefficiency in the provision of public goods?
questions.explanation:
The primary reason a free market fails to efficiently provide public goods is the free-riding problem.

 Because public goods are non-excludable, individuals can consume the good without paying for it (free-ride), leading to little incentive for private firms to produce them, resulting in under-provision.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following microeconomic policy involves by which the government manipulates its expenditure and revenue side?
questions.explanation:
Fiscal policy is the tool where the government uses its spending (expenditure) and taxation (revenue) powers to influence the economy.

 It is the primary way the government directly affects aggregate demand.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following instrument is considered by the contractionary fiscal policy when there is an excess demand and inflationary pressure in the economy?
questions.explanation:
Contractionary fiscal policy is used to reduce Aggregate Demand (AD), which is necessary when there is excess demand and inflationary pressure.

 The tools for this are decreasing government expenditure (spending) or increasing taxes (revenue). A decrease in expenditure directly reduces AD.

questions.questionText: A tight monetary policy is applied in circumstance where there is
questions.explanation:
Tight monetary policy (or contractionary monetary policy) is used to cool down an overheated economy by raising interest rates and reducing the money supply.

 This is typically done to combat High inflation, which is often caused by excessive aggregate demand.

questions.questionText: 19) If tight fiscal and monetary policies fail to address the problem of rising price level, what is the alternative policy that the government should consider?
questions.explanation:
If traditional demand-side policies (fiscal and monetary) are ineffective against inflation, a government may turn to Income policy.

 This involves direct intervention in the wage and price setting process—such as wage and price controls or guidelines—to slow the inflation rate by targeting the underlying costs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following exchange rate regime is the one determined by the government political and economic decisions?
questions.explanation:
A Fixed exchange rate regime is one where the government (or central bank) sets and actively maintains a specific value for its currency relative to another currency or a basket of currencies.

 This value is a political and economic decision of the government, which then commits to defending that rate using its reserves.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following difference is the cause for efficiency loss in the presence of negative externalities?
options: Between marginal social benefits and marginal private benefits
Between marginal social cost and marginal private cost
Between private marginal cost and marginal external cost
Between private marginal benefits and marginal external benefits
questions.explanation:
A negative externality (like pollution from production) means the Marginal Social Cost (MSC) is greater than the Marginal Private Cost (MPC).

 The difference is the marginal external cost. Because producers only consider the MPC, they overproduce relative to the social optimum, leading to an efficiency loss (deadweight loss).

questions.questionText: When insurance company provides fringe benefit and marginal benefits on the basis of an average rate over set of employees and guarantee them to participate in the program, then this can see as solution for which one of the following problem?
questions.explanation:
This mandatory, group-based insurance is a solution for Adverse selection. Adverse selection occurs when only high-risk people choose to buy insurance.

 By guaranteeing participation for a whole group, the insurer pools both high- and low-risk individuals, making the average rate sustainable.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following macroeconomic policies involves management of money supply and interest rate?
questions.explanation:
Monetary policy is the action undertaken by a central bank to manipulate the money supply and interest rates to stimulate or contract the economy.

 Fiscal policy involves government spending and taxation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the monetary policy tool that involves the purchase and sale of securities by the nation's central bank?
questions.explanation:
Open Market Operations (OMO), which is the buying and selling of government securities (bonds) by the central bank, is the most frequently used and flexible tool of monetary policy.

 Buying securities increases the money supply; selling securities decreases it.

questions.questionText: 25) Which one of the following is considered to be fiscal policy tool? Which one is it?
questions.explanation:
Fiscal policy involves the government using its revenue and expenditure to influence the economy.

 Taxation is the primary way the government collects revenue, making it a key fiscal policy tool.

 Transfer payments and Grants in aid are types of government expenditure, which is the other side of fiscal policy.

questions.questionText: 26) Which one of the following is correct about price ceiling?
options: It is one of the income policies that keeps a price from declining from certain limit
It is a maximizing price set by law to make a basic consumption goods affordable to buyers
It should be set above the equilibrium price to make it more effective
It is discourages consumers from buying goods and services since they are now paying higher prices.
questions.explanation:
A price ceiling is a maximum legal price set by the government, typically for necessities like rent or basic food items.

 Its purpose is to keep prices from rising above the set limit, making essential goods affordable for consumers.

 To be effective (binding), it must be set below the equilibrium price.

questions.questionText: 27) Suppose the value of an Ethiopian Birr in terms of Kenya shilling is getting higher. What is the impact of this on the Ethiopian export to Kenya?
options: It will make the price of Ethiopian goods in the Kenya market cheaper
It will make the price of Kenyan import in the Ethiopian market expensive.
It will increase Ethiopia's export earning
It will reduce Ethiopia's export earning
questions.explanation:
If the value of the Ethiopian Birr is getting higher (it is appreciating), then each Birr can buy more Kenyan Shillings.

 This means Ethiopian goods are now*more expensive for Kenyan buyers, leading to a decrease in Ethiopian exports to Kenya. Consequently, this will reduce Ethiopia's export earning.

questions.questionText: 28) Which one of the following clearly define taxation?
options: It is the only source of government revenue
It is levied without anything in direct return
questions.explanation:
Taxation is a compulsory levy by a government on persons or property to raise revenue.

 The defining characteristic is that it is collected without anything in direct return to the payer (it is a non-quid pro quo payment, unlike a user fee).

questions.questionText: 29) Which one of the following explains the tax principles called "canon of economy"?
options: Everyone should pay tax according to his ability
The amount of tax that we are supposed to pay should be known in advance.
Every tax payer should pay the tax in his own convenient
The cost of tax collection should be as minimum as possible.
questions.explanation:
Adam Smith's Canons of Taxation include the canon of economy (or efficiency).

 This principle states that the cost of collecting the tax (the administrative costs for the government) and the compliance costs for the taxpayer should be as minimal as possible relative to the revenue collected.

questions.questionText: 30) Which one of the following is the implication one a good tax is referred to as broad bases?
options: The system should impose tax on all people without discrimination
The system should ensure that an income inequality is reduced
The system should impose tax on income and properties and commodities
The system should ascertain that national income and living standard is increasing.
questions.explanation:
A tax with broad bases (or base coverage) means that the tax is applied to a wide range of economic activities, transactions, or assets.

 This includes taxes on income, property, and commodities (consumption).

 A broad base typically allows the government to generate sufficient revenue with lower tax rates.

questions.questionText: 31) Which one of the following is the advantages of fiscal decentralization?
options: Provide scale economies in the collection of taxes
Provide scale economies in the provision of public goods
provision of public goods and services desired by the local residents
questions.explanation:
A key advantage of fiscal decentralization is that local governments can tailor the provision of public goods and services to better match the specific needs and preferences of the local residents.

 Centralized systems often result in uniform provision that doesn't account for regional differences.

questions.questionText: 32) One of the following is considered to be the aim of fiscal decentralization? Which one is it?
options: Enhancing the role of private sector
questions.explanation: The overarching goals of fiscal decentralization are to improve both efficiency (by matching local provision to local preferences) and equity (by addressing regional disparities in resources and service access, often through central transfers).

questions.questionText: 33) Which one of the following is the reason for the federal government to make fiscal equalization payment to local governments?
options: To encourage innovation in those goods and service provided locally
To narrow regional gaps in the provision of basic public services
questions.explanation:
Fiscal equalization payments are central government transfers designed to ensure that all sub-national governments, regardless of their local revenue capacity, can provide a comparable level of basic public services to their citizens.

 The primary goal is to narrow regional gaps in service provision, thereby promoting vertical and horizontal equity.

questions.questionText: 34) What is the reason for growing needs for the conservation of environmental resources?
options: Most of these resource are infinite
questions.explanation:
The primary reason for the growing need for conservation is that many environmental resources are finite (non-renewable) or are being depleted/degraded at an unsustainable rate.

 Scarcity necessitates conservation to ensure long-term availability.

questions.questionText: 35) What was the cause for rising greenhouse gases in the earth's atmosphere?
options: A decrease in afforestation due to government policy
The decomposition and disposal of waste
questions.explanation:
While the burning of fossil fuels is the largest contributor to rising greenhouse gases (GHGs), among the given options, The decomposition and disposal of waste (especially in landfills) produces significant amounts of methane (CH4), which is a powerful GHG.

 Afforestation (planting trees) reduces CO2, and hydropower generation is a low-emission energy source.

questions.questionText: 36) Among the following direct taxes, which one is a tax that is imposed on the land and building?
questions.explanation:
A Property tax (also called a real estate tax or millage rate) is an ad valorem tax assessed on the value of property, such as land and buildings.

 It is typically a direct tax, as the burden cannot be shifted.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an objective of taxation?
questions.explanation:
One of the primary objectives of taxation is to achieve equity and reduce income disparity.

 Governments use progressive tax systems, where higher earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes, and then use the collected revenue for social programs and subsidies, aiming to redistribute wealth and narrow the gap between the rich and the poor. The other options are generally not objectives of taxation; for example, taxation is often used to *discourage* consumption of harmful products (like tobacco and alcohol) through excise taxes.

questions.questionText: The burden and incident is imposed by one of the following tax categories on different individual. Which one is it?
questions.explanation: Payroll tax is imposed on wages and salaries, and its economic burden can be shared between employers and employees, so it affects different individuals differently.}

questions.questionText: In Ethiopia, which one of the following institution is responsible to collect tax on behalf of the government?
questions.explanation:
In Ethiopia, the primary governmental institution responsible for the assessment and collection of federal taxes and duties is the Ministry of Revenue.

 This body oversees the tax system and its administration.

questions.questionText: Which one is the type of indirect tax imposed on luxury items and other goods that are inelastic when the goods is imported?
questions.explanation:
An Excise Tax is a tax on the production, sale, or consumption of specific goods or services, like luxury items, alcohol, and tobacco.

 They are often applied to goods with inelastic demand (meaning consumers will buy them even if the price increases) or for regulatory/social purposes.

 Unlike VAT, which is broad, excise taxes target specific items. While Customs Duty (not listed as an option but related) is a tax on imports, the specific tax imposed based on the *nature* of the good (luxury, inelastic) is the excise tax.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains climate change?
options: It refer to an average weather pattern ever many years
It is expressed in terms of daily changes in the rainfall and humidity
It is a short term changes in the atmosphere conditions
It is the problem of the developed world only
questions.explanation:
Climate change refers to a long-term shift in temperatures and weather patterns. Climate is generally defined as the average weather pattern of a region observed over an extended period, typically 30 years or more.

 Options B and C describe weather, which is the short-term state of the atmosphere. Option D is incorrect, as climate change is a global issue that severely impacts developing countries as well.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following indicates the direct health dimension of the impacts of the climate change?
questions.explanation:
The direct health dimension refers to effects that immediately and explicitly impact human health.

 Malaria is a disease transmitted by mosquitos, and climate change (specifically rising temperatures and altered rainfall patterns) can expand the geographic range and seasonality of mosquito vectors, directly increasing the incidence of the disease.

 Drought and water shortage are environmental impacts that can indirectly affect health (through famine or poor hygiene), and deforestation is an environmental change, but Malaria is a direct health outcome.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is said to have more than 20% contribution to harmful greenhouse gas emission in the developing countries?
questions.explanation:
In many developing countries, Deforestation (part of the Land Use Change and Forestry sector) is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions, often contributing more than 20% of the national total.

 This is due to the conversion of forests for agriculture, logging, or urbanization, which releases stored carbon into the atmosphere. While burning fossil fuel is the largest global source, deforestation plays a proportionally greater role in the emissions profiles of many developing nations.

questions.questionText: The effect that poor developing economies exerts to bring growth and development in jeopardized due to
options: Lack of support of adaption from the developed countries
Allocation of a good proportion of their budget to finance adoption
High dependence on climate insensitive resources
Absence of mitigation and adoption mechanism.
questions.explanation:
The efforts of developing economies to achieve growth and development are often undermined because of their high dependence on climate-sensitive resources (like rain-fed agriculture, water resources, and natural ecosystems) and limited economic diversification.

 Climate change impacts like drought, flooding, and shifting seasons directly damage these core sectors, thereby jeopardizing their development gains.

 While options A and D are also challenges, the vulnerability created by reliance on climate-sensitive sectors (Option C) makes their development goals intrinsically fragile.

questions.questionText: What action been taken by the government to address climate change problems in Ethiopia?
options: Implementation of climate resilient green economy facility
Taxes on carbon emission to avoid the problem of climate change
Provision of incentives to encourage technological progress
Achieving economic growth and development in any possible ways.
questions.explanation:
The Ethiopian government launched the Climate-Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) Strategy in 2011. This strategy aims to achieve middle-income status by 2025 while building a green economy that is resilient to climate change.

 Therefore, the Implementation of a climate resilient green economy facility (or strategy) is the specific, high-level policy action taken by the Ethiopian government to address climate change and development simultaneously.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following features characterizes the National Development plan during the Derg Period?
options: The main development strategy was agriculture led development
questions.explanation: During the Derg (P-M-A-C) regime in Ethiopia, the government's economic policy was Marxist-Leninist, involving nationalization and state control. A key feature of this period in agriculture was the formation and promotion of producer and service cooperatives to replace private farming, aiming for collective ownership and cultivation of land.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the key priority area that is considered to be the basis for the locally developed economic reform program recently?
questions.explanation:
Ethiopia's recent economic reform program places a strong emphasis on addressing structural constraints and ensuring equitable growth.

 While all options are relevant to long-term development, Sustainable rural development is often cited as a key foundational pillar in Ethiopia's planning, given the large size of its rural, agriculture-dependent population.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following factor is the one that necessitated the formation of the home-growth economic reform in Ethiopia?
options: The crowding out public investment by private investment
The failure of gradual transition from private public sector led growth
Failure to create additional job opportunities
questions.explanation: The home-grown economic reform in Ethiopia was necessitated by the failure of the previous gradual transition from a public-private sector-led growth model, which did not achieve sustainable and inclusive economic development.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is duly emphasized in one of the home growth economic called sectorial reform in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation:
The Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda includes significant **sectoral reforms** aimed at transforming the economy.

 A core area of emphasis is the Service sector, particularly in high-value areas like logistics, tourism, and Information and Communications Technology (ICT), to diversify the economy and boost exports. (Note: While tourism is important, the reform focuses on the broader service sector transformation.)

questions.questionText: Which one of the three home-growth economic reforms is mainly concerned with minimizing external loan and rescheduling the existing external public debt?
questions.explanation:
The Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda is generally divided into Macroeconomic, Structural, and Sectoral reforms.

 Issues related to external debt management, minimizing borrowing, and stabilizing the currency and overall economy fall under the scope of Macroeconomic reform.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following indicates the rank of Ethiopia in its human development despite the effort made to reduce the headcount poverty over the past twenty years?
questions.explanation:
Despite significant progress in reducing the headcount poverty ratio (the percentage of the population below the poverty line) and improving other poverty indicators over the past two decades, Ethiopia's overall ranking on the global Human Development Index (HDI) remains low.

 The HDI is a composite index measuring life expectancy, education, and per capita income, and a Low human development index indicates persistent challenges in improving these non-income dimensions of development.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the common feature of both 'Ider' and 'Iqub'?
options: In both, members assist each other on a rotational basis
In both, the strong ties among members encourage defaults
questions.explanation:
Ider (traditional burial society) and Iqub (rotating savings and credit association or ROSCA) are both informal financial mechanisms common in Ethiopia.

 The key common feature is that members contribute regularly, and the pooled resource (money for Iqub, or support/funds for Ider) is distributed among members on a rotational or need-based basis, signifying mutual social and financial assistance.

questions.questionText: What was the objectives of the first five years development plan that was formulated during the imperial era from 1957 to 1961?
options: Promotion of industries aiming towards export
questions.explanation:
Ethiopia's First Five-Year Plan (1957-1961), formulated during the Imperial Era, primarily focused on developing the economic infrastructure and encouraging the modernization of key sectors.

 A major objective was the **Promotion of commercial agriculture** to move beyond subsistence farming and increase exports, thereby generating foreign exchange for industrial investment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following development plan of the imperial period had more focus on the agricultural sector to address the problem of increasing food shortages?
questions.explanation: The First Five-Year Plan (1957–1961) of imperial Ethiopia primarily focused on agriculture to increase food production and reduce shortages. Subsequent plans, such as the Second Five-Year Plan, shifted focus more toward industry and infrastructure rather than directly addressing agricultural food shortages.

questions.questionText: In Ethiopia which one of the following has got particular attention in the past yet characterized as the lowest productive in its performance?
questions.explanation:
The Agricultural sector has historically been the primary focus of development plans in Ethiopia due to its large share in employment and GDP.

 However, due to reliance on traditional methods, rain-fed farming, and limited use of technology, it is often characterized as the lowest in terms of productivity (output per unit of input or labor) compared to other sectors and global averages.

questions.questionText: What does the Gini coefficient of 1 represent?
options: All income owned by one person
questions.explanation:
The Gini coefficient is a measure of statistical dispersion intended to represent the income or wealth distribution of a nation's residents, and is the most commonly used measure of inequality.

 A Gini coefficient of 0 represents perfect equality (everyone has the same income).

 A Gini coefficient of 1 (or 100%) represents maximum inequality, where theoretically **all income is owned by one person** (or one household).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following country has made great success in lifting millions of people out of poverty in the last three decades?
questions.explanation:
Over the last three decades, China has achieved the most rapid and massive reduction in poverty in world history.

 Through rapid economic growth and effective government policies, it has lifted hundreds of millions of people out of extreme poverty, making it a globally recognized success story in poverty reduction.

questions.questionText: What is the reason for extreme poverty to remain a challenge in Sub-Saharan African countries?
options: Lack of growth and development plans
questions.explanation:
Extreme poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is a complex challenge, but a fundamental economic issue is the Lack of growth and development plans that can generate sustained, inclusive, and job-creating economic expansion.

 While the region has had plans, their successful implementation and ability to generate transformative growth have often been insufficient to escape the poverty trap.

questions.questionText: What is the reason for women to existence extreme poverty in the developing world?
options: The earning capacity of women is high
Their control over their spouses' income is limited
Their access to the formal sector employment is high
questions.explanation:
Women in developing countries often face limited control over household resources and income, which restricts their economic autonomy.

 This lack of control, combined with social and cultural constraints, contributes significantly to their vulnerability to extreme poverty.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is among the measure that should not be considered to alleviate the problem of poverty facing women?
options: Adoption of policy that integrates women in various programs and influences their welfare
Increasing female participation in education and other training programs
Enhancing female participation in formal sector employment
Discouraging women activity in agricultural extension programs
questions.explanation:
Poverty alleviation strategies focus on empowering women economically and socially. Measures like integrating women into programs, increasing education, and enhancing formal sector employment (A, B, and C) all directly improve women's welfare and earning capacity. 

Discouraging women activity in agricultural extension programs (D) would be counterproductive, as it would reduce their access to vital knowledge and technology needed to improve productivity and income in the sector where most rural women work.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following expresses the classical views?
options: The economy will move towards full employment of GDP
Expansionary fiscal or monetary policy is necessary
Demand side policies only affect the real wage, employment and output
Monetary policy has effects on the real sphere of the economy
questions.explanation: Classical economists believe in the **self-regulating nature of markets** and flexible prices and wages. This view holds that any deviation from full employment is temporary, and the economy will naturally adjust back to its potential level, meaning **The economy will move towards full employment of GDP** in the long run. Options B and C are primarily Keynesian or New Classical views.

questions.questionText: What is the important lesson the world has learnt from the 1930's Great Depression?
options: The self-correcting feature of the market works
The additional government spending will stimulate unemployment
The possibility of the real GDP to fall below the potential FDP is nil
questions.explanation:
The Great Depression demonstrated the failure of the market's self-correcting mechanisms, challenging the Classical view (Option A).

 The sustained high unemployment and deep recession showed that economies could remain stuck below potential for long periods.

 The key lesson, popularized by Keynesian economics, was The importance active stabilization policies (fiscal and monetary) by the government to quickly restore full employment and stabilize output.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following schools of thought suggested that the Central Bank should follow a constant growth rule for some monetary aggregate to address macroeconomic problems?
questions.explanation:
Monetarism, prominently associated with Milton Friedman, argues that inflation is primarily a monetary phenomenon.

 They suggested that the Central Bank should avoid discretionary policy and instead follow a predictable constant money growth rule (e.g., keeping the money supply growth rate stable and equal to the long-run GDP growth rate) to achieve price stability and macroeconomic stability.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the component of aggregate demand that includes private purchase of the structures, equipments and accumulation of inventories?
questions.explanation:
Aggregate Demand (AD) is calculated as C + I + G + X - M.

 The component that covers private spending on capital goods (equipment, structures, and new housing) and changes in stock (inventory accumulation) is Investment (I).

questions.questionText: In macroeconomics the current consumption expenditure is likely increase due to?
options: Expectation of lower price in the future
questions.explanation:
Consumption expenditure is positively related to expected future income. If households Expectation of higher future income, they feel wealthier and more secure, leading them to increase their current spending and reduce their current saving.

 Options A, B, and C would all generally cause a decrease in current consumption.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a branch of economic that studies about the aggregate behavior of the economy?
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics is the branch of economics that deals with the performance, structure, behavior, and decision-making of an economy as a whole (aggregate variables), including national income, growth, inflation, and unemployment.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is macroeconomic issues?
options: Action of an individual agent within an economy
The economic activities of a consumers, a producer or industry
Resource allocation or price determination as central problem
Structure and performance of the economy as a whole
questions.explanation:
Macroeconomics focuses on the aggregate behavior of the economy. Issues like inflation, unemployment, and economic growth are studied by analyzing the Structure and performance of the economy as a whole.

 Options A, B, and C relate to microeconomics, which studies individual decisions and specific markets.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is used to calculate GDP by adding all the incomes accruing to all factors of production used in producing the national output?
questions.explanation:
There are three main ways to calculate GDP. The Income Approach calculates GDP by summing up all the income generated by production, which includes wages (for labor), rent (for land), interest (for capital), and profits (for entrepreneurship/capital).

 This corresponds to 'adding all the incomes accruing to all factors of production'.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following characterizes period of expansion in the business cycles?
options: The pressure of prices is upward
Full employment occurs at this stage
questions.explanation:
An expansion is a phase of the business cycle characterized by increasing economic activity, rising GDP, and falling unemployment.

 As the economy nears its peak capacity during an expansion, demand often outstrips supply, putting upward pressure on prices, leading to inflation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the market values of country's exports and import of goods and services are shown?
questions.explanation:
The Current Account is the section of the Balance of Payments (BOP) that records a country's trade balance (exports and imports of goods and services), net factor income (income earned from abroad), and net transfers.

 It specifically tracks the value of exports and imports of goods and services.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the problem of taxation in Ethiopia that is considered to be legal from the point of view of law but poses problems on the tax administration?
questions.explanation:
Tax avoidance refers to the legal use of the tax regime to one's own advantage, to reduce the amount of tax that is payable by means and schemes that are within the law.

 While legal, it narrows the tax base and creates complex challenges for the **tax administration** to monitor and enforce, as opposed to Tax evasion (A) which is illegal.

questions.questionText: What remedial solutions do you think should be put in the place to alleviate tax collection problem in Ethiopia?
options: Provide client oriented service to tax payers
Lowering the tax rate far below the current rate
questions.explanation: Improving tax administration by providing client-oriented services (such as simplifying procedures, improving transparency, and enhancing taxpayer support) encourages compliance and reduces problems in tax collection.

questions.questionText: The World Bank define poverty as 'the pronounced deprivation in the wellbeing'. Which one of the following is NOT the implication of wellbeing?
options: The poor are those who do not have any control over commodities
It relates poverty with some specific types of consumption
It relates to lack of key capability to function in the society
Poverty is the only about the lack of one thing, food
questions.explanation:
The World Bank's definition of poverty as 'pronounced deprivation in the wellbeing' is a multidimensional concept.

 It implies a lack of health, education, security, and voice (Options A, B, and C can be related to this broad view).

 Option D, which states that Poverty is only about the lack of one thing, food, is explicitly incorrect because the definition goes far beyond mere caloric intake to include non-monetary deprivations, such as lack of capability and opportunity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a Uni dimensional measure of poverty that helps to understand the degree of income inequality among the poor?
questions.explanation: The Total Poverty Gap measures the aggregate shortfall of income among the poor relative to the poverty line. It is a uni-dimensional measure that captures both the incidence and the depth of poverty, helping to understand income inequality among the poor.

questions.questionText: One of the following shows the proportion of total national incomes that factors of productions receives, which one is it?
questions.explanation:
The Functional distribution of income shows how the total national income is divided among the various factors of production (land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship).

 In other words, it measures the proportion of income that goes to wages, rent, interest, and profits. This is distinct from the size or personal distribution, which looks at how income is distributed among individual households.

questions.questionText: Consider a hypothetical economy in which a consumer buys 2 kg of apples and 5 kg of oranges at the prices of birr 150 and 70 per kg respectively in 2016 E.C. If in 2015 E.C the prices of these two goods, apples and oranges were 125 and 55 birr per kg respectively, then what is the rate of inflation during the year 2016 E.C assuming that 2015 E.C is base year?
questions.explanation:
To calculate the inflation rate, first compute total expenditure in the base year (2015 E.C): 2 kg of apples * 125 = 250, 5 kg of oranges * 55 = 275, total = 525.

 Then compute total expenditure in 2016 E.C: 2 kg of apples * 150 = 300, 5 kg of oranges * 70 = 350, total = 650.

 The inflation rate = ((650 - 525) / 525) * 100 = 23.81%,

 which corresponds to option B 23.80%.

questions.questionText: Suppose that the nominal wage that the firms has agreed to pay for worker is birr 60 per hour. What is the change in the real wage rate if the price level as measure by the price index increase from 2.50 to 3.00?
options: The real wage rises by 4 birr
The real wage decline by 4 birr
The real wage declined by 6 birr
The real wage rises by 6 birr
questions.explanation:
The real wage is calculated as nominal wage divided by the price index. Initial real wage = 60 / 2.5 = 24 birr per hour.

 New real wage = 60 / 3 = 20 birr per hour.

 Change in real wage = 20 - 24 = -4 birr, meaning the real wage declined by 4 birr.

 Therefore, the correct answer is option B.

questions.questionText: Gemechu is employed in Ethiopia public institution and monthly gross salary is 18,000 Birr. How much is his net income after paying employment income tax?
questions.explanation: Assuming Ethiopia's employment income tax rate is 26% for this salary bracket: Tax = 18,000 × 0.26 = 4,680 Birr. Net income = 18,000 - 4,680 = 13,320 Birr. The closest option is A: 13,200 Birr.

questions.questionText: Suppose in a given economy the population who are willing and able to work is 5 million and out of this the total number of employed are 2 million. What is the unemployment rate?

A census that was conducted in a particular economy shows that the total adult population is 27 million and those who are willing and able to work is 6 million. What is the labor force participation in the economy?
questions.explanation:
Labor force participation rate = (Labor force / Adult population) × 100 =

 (6,000,000 / 27,000,000) × 100 ≈ 22.22%.

questions.questionText: The concept of Adverse Selection in insurance markets is a consequence of:
options: Asymmetric information before a transaction occurs.
questions.explanation: Adverse selection occurs when one party in a transaction (e.g., the insurance buyer) has more relevant information than the other (the insurer) before the transaction, leading to the selection of high-risk customers.

questions.questionText: What is the primary objective of a government issuing a Bond to the public?
options: To increase the money supply in the economy.
To raise funds to finance budget deficits or public spending.
To decrease interest rates in the economy.
questions.explanation: Governments sell bonds to borrow money from the public and institutions. This is a primary method for financing government expenditure and closing a budget deficit.

questions.questionText: The difference between Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Gross National Product (GNP) is:
questions.explanation:
GNP = GDP + NFIA.
 NFIA is the income earned by domestic factors of production from abroad minus the income earned by foreign factors of production domestically.

questions.questionText: To combat a severe recession and high unemployment, the government implements an Expansionary Fiscal Policy. This would most likely involve:
options: Decreasing government spending and increasing taxes.
Increasing government spending and decreasing taxes.
Selling government bonds to commercial banks.
Increasing the central bank's policy interest rate.
questions.explanation: Expansionary fiscal policy aims to boost Aggregate Demand (AD). This is achieved by increasing G (a direct component of AD) and/or decreasing T (which increases disposable income and thus consumption, C).

questions.questionText: The 'Free-Rider Problem' is most commonly associated with:
questions.explanation:
The Free-Rider Problem arises with public goods because of their non-excludable nature.
 People can benefit from the good without paying for it, leading to under-provision of the good by the private sector.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about nominal GDP and real GDP?
options: Nominal GDP values goods and services at current price.
Nominal GDP is GDP adjusted for price changes.
Real GDP values goods and services at current price.
Nominal is GDP computed using a base year price.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP evaluates an economy's total production of goods and services using current-period market prices.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the contribution of the service sector in the Ethiopian Economy over the last two decades?
options: Its employment contribution is largest next to the industrial sector.
Its large contribution to the GDP comes from government employment.
Its contribution to foreign exchange earning has been decreasing overtime.
Its achievements have been mainly reflected in areas of wholesale trade.
questions.explanation: In Ethiopia's service sector growth over recent decades, distributive trade services—specifically wholesale and retail trade—have accounted for a significant share of economic activity.

questions.questionText: The consumer is in equilibrium when the Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS) is equal to the ratio of the two goods' prices. This is represented by:
options: The budget line is tangent to the highest possible indifference curve.
The indifference curve is intersecting the budget line.
The total utility is at its maximum.
The budget line is at the origin.
questions.explanation: Consumer equilibrium under the ordinal utility approach is achieved at the point where the slope of the indifference curve (MRS) equals the slope of the budget line (price ratio), which is the point of tangency.

questions.questionText: Total spending in the economy rises from one year to the next due to either the economy is producing a larger output or outputs are being sold at higher prices. To measure these effects, economists use real GDP and Nominal GDP. Which one of the following is correct about the two measures?
options: Change in real GDP reflects only changes in the amounts being produced.
Nominal GDP values the economy's production of goods and services at a constant base year price.
Change in nominal GDP reflects only changes in the amounts being produced.
Real GDP values the economy's production of goods and services at current price.
questions.explanation: Real GDP evaluates output using constant prices from a base year, meaning changes in real GDP accurately reflect only physical changes in the quantity of output produced.

questions.questionText: If a government wants to reduce income inequality through its fiscal policy, it should primarily use:
questions.explanation: A progressive tax system requires higher-income earners to pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes, which is a standard method for redistributing wealth and reducing inequality.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a Direct Tax?
questions.explanation: Direct taxes are levied on the income or wealth of a person, and the burden cannot be shifted to another party (e.g., employment income tax, business profit tax). Indirect taxes (VAT, Sales, Excise) are levied on goods and services.

questions.questionText: If the Ethiopian Birr (ETB) appreciates against the US Dollar (USD), holding other factors constant, this typically leads to:
options: decrease in the price of Ethiopian exports in USD.
An increase in the price of US imports in ETB.
An increase in the price of US imports in USD.
decrease in the price of US imports in ETB.
questions.explanation: Birr appreciation means one ETB buys more USD. This makes Ethiopian exports more expensive for US buyers and US imports cheaper for Ethiopian buyers. The price of US imports in ETB will decrease.

questions.questionText: In the short run, a large increase in government spending will cause the Aggregate Demand (AD) curve to:
questions.explanation:
Government spending (G) is a component of Aggregate Demand (AD = C + I + G + Xn).
 An increase in G directly increases AD, causing the AD curve to shift to the right.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the relationship between consumption and saving?
options: When income is more than consumption there is a positive saving.
When income equals to consumption there is a positive saving.
When income is more than consumption there is a dissaving.
When income is less than consumption there is a positive saving.
questions.explanation:
Saving is defined as disposable income minus consumption (S = Y - C).

 When income exceeds consumption (Y > C), saving is positive.

questions.questionText: In the Expenditure Approach to calculating GDP, which component accounts for spending by households on final goods and services?
questions.explanation:
The Expenditure Approach formula is GDP = C + I + G + Xn.
 'C' stands for Personal Consumption Expenditure.

questions.questionText: The quantity of money that commercial banks must keep at the Central Bank, which cannot be loaned out, is determined by the:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Requirement (or reserve ratio) dictates the fraction of deposits that banks must hold as reserves, thereby controlling the money multiplier.

questions.questionText: Suppose the planning expert wants to measure the GDP of the country using alternative approaches by including all the necessary components in each approach. Which one of the following statements is correct about the components of approaches?
options: In expenditure approach, we add the returns of factors of production to measure GDP.
The income approach of GDP accounting represents the demand for final goods and services.
In the product approach GDP is estimated by calculating the value added at each stage of production.
Rent and profit payments are components of the value-added approach of measuring GDP.
questions.explanation: The product (or value-added) approach measures GDP by summing the value added (output minus intermediate consumption) at each stage of production across all industries.

questions.questionText: A factory's pollution harms the health of nearby residents, but the factory does not pay for the damages. This situation is a classic example of:
questions.explanation: A negative externality of production occurs when the production process imposes an uncompensated cost (e.g., pollution, health issues) on a third party.

questions.questionText: Gemechu owns a sole proprietorship type of business and incurred a loss. Which one of the following could result in the sale of his private house if his business assets are not enough to cover the business liabilities?
options: Not suitable for large scale operations
questions.explanation: Under unlimited liability, a sole proprietor is personally responsible for all business debts, meaning personal assets (like a private house) can be seized to pay off unpaid liabilities.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the budget line?
options: It shows the optimal combination of two goods that the consumer can buy when his or her income changes.
It shows the various combinations of two commodities which give equal satisfaction to the consumer.
It shows different combinations of two goods that a consumer can buy with a given income at a given price.
It shows the locus of points representing various combinations of the two commodities purchased by the consumer.
questions.explanation: A budget line represents all possible combinations of two goods that a consumer can purchase given a fixed income level and prevailing market prices.
